questions.question: Give three ways the weather affects what people wear, their homes and their food.
questions.expected_answer: On hot days people wear light, loose, light-coloured clothes and hats, and on cold or rainy days warm layers and raincoats. Homes in hot places have verandas, shade and breezes, while homes in cold places need heaters and blankets. Farmers depend on rain at the right time, and drought, hail and frost can ruin crops.

questions.question: Explain how weather affects travel and work.
questions.expected_answer: Heavy rain makes roads slippery and floods low bridges, mist makes it hard to see, snow closes mountain passes, and storms delay planes and ships. Outdoor workers such as builders, farmers and sellers depend on good weather, and storms can cause power cuts that affect homes and businesses.

questions.question: How can people stay safe in extreme weather?
questions.expected_answer: Listen to weather warnings from the South African Weather Service. In heatwaves, drink water, stay in the shade and wear hats and sunscreen. In thunderstorms, stay indoors, away from water and tall trees. Never walk, swim or drive through floodwater. In a drought, save water.
